q: Under the leave rules, a spell of leave of a railway servant ordinarily begins and ends as under:

options.A: It begins on the day on which charge is relinquished and ends on the day on which charge is resumed
options.B: It begins on the first day of the month in which it is sanctioned and ends on the last day of that month
options.C: It begins on the day following the day on which charge of the post is relinquished and ends on the day preceding the day on which charge is resumed
options.D: It begins and ends on the dates entered in the leave application, irrespective of the relinquishing or resumption of charge

e: Leave ordinarily begins on the day following the day charge is relinquished and ends on the day preceding the day charge is resumed, under the leave rules.

q: The Reporting Officer has not had an opportunity to observe the work and conduct of a railway servant for the minimum prescribed period during the report year. The correct course in regard to his Annual Performance Appraisal Report for that year is to:

options.A: Write the report on the basis of the report of the previous year
options.B: Record a 'No Report Certificate' in the report for that year
options.C: Award a 'Good' grading to the railway servant by default
options.D: Obtain the report from the recognised trade union of the cadre

e: If the Reporting Officer has not observed the work for the minimum prescribed period, a No Report Certificate is recorded in the APAR for that year.

q: The currency, that is, the period of validity, of a panel formed on the Railways for promotion to a selection post is ordinarily:

options.A: Two years, or till the panel is exhausted, whichever is earlier
options.B: One year, or till the panel is exhausted, whichever is earlier
options.C: Five years from the date of its formation
options.D: Unlimited, till all the empanelled railway servants are promoted

e: The currency of a panel for a selection post is ordinarily two years, or till the panel is exhausted, whichever is earlier.

q: A railway servant finds that his position in the published seniority list of his category is not correct. Under the Indian Railway Establishment Manual, he may represent against his position as shown in the list within:
e: Under IREM, a servant may represent against his position in the published seniority list within one year.

q: A railway servant drawing basic pay of Rs 33,000 per month is posted in a city classified as 'Y' class for the purpose of House Rent Allowance. Dearness Allowance has crossed 25 per cent, so that House Rent Allowance in a 'Y' class city is payable at 18 per cent of basic pay. The House Rent Allowance admissible to him per month will be:
e: For a Y class city, HRA is 18 per cent of basic pay when DA has crossed 25 per cent. So 18 per cent of Rs 33,000 = Rs 5,940.

q: Under the General Departmental Competitive Examination scheme on the Railways, serving railway employees who fulfil the prescribed qualifications and age conditions are permitted to compete for vacancies in the direct recruitment quota of the specified posts to the extent of:
e: Under GDCE, serving employees may compete for 25 per cent of the vacancies in the direct recruitment quota of the specified posts.

q: Promotion to the posts of Senior Section Officer (Accounts), Senior Travelling Inspector of Accounts and Senior Inspector of Station Accounts is made on passing the qualifying departmental examination of the Accounts Department known as the:
e: Promotion to Senior Section Officer (Accounts), Senior TIA and Senior ISA is on passing the Appendix III examination of the Accounts Department.

q: A Group 'B' officer wishes to view and submit his Annual Performance Appraisal Report online. The online system used on the Railways for recording and processing the APARs of gazetted officers is:
e: SPARROW is the online system used on the Railways for recording and processing APARs of gazetted officers.

q: The Centralised Pension Grievances Redress and Monitoring System, through which railway pensioners can lodge and track grievances relating to their pension matters online, is known as:
e: CPENGRAMS is the Centralised Pension Grievances Redress and Monitoring System for railway pensioners to lodge and track pension grievances online.

q: A retiring officer wishes to place on record, on an online platform, his experiences and suggestions from his years of service for the benefit of the administration. That platform is:
e: Anubhav is the online platform where a retiring officer records his experiences and suggestions from service for the benefit of the administration.

q: A serving clerk wishes to lodge a service grievance online and track its disposal. The online facility provided on the Railways for redressal of the grievances of serving employees is:
e: Nivaran is the online facility on the Railways for redressal of grievances of serving employees, with facility to track disposal.

q: In a meeting on staff participation, an officer refers to the forum 'PREM' functioning on the Railways for consultation with railway employees. The letters PREM stand for:

options.C: Panel of Railway Experts and Managers
options.D: Participation of Railway Employees in Management

e: PREM stands for Participation of Railway Employees in Management, the forum for consultation with railway employees on the Railways.

q: A matter concerning railway employees generally is to be taken up under the Joint Consultative Machinery at the national level. It is dealt with in:

options.B: The Permanent Negotiating Machinery at the Railway Board level
options.C: The Staff Council of the Zonal Railway
options.D: The National Council of the Joint Consultative Machinery alone

e: Matters concerning railway employees generally under the Joint Consultative Machinery at the national level are dealt with in the Departmental Council (Railways).

q: A proposal is made that the General Manager should personally administer the Staff Benefit Fund of a zonal Railway without any committee. Under the rules, the Fund is administered:

options.A: Personally by the General Manager of each zonal Railway, without any committee
options.B: By the Railway Recruitment Boards of the respective zones
options.C: By the recognised trade unions of railway employees alone
options.D: Through Staff Benefit Fund Committees constituted at the prescribed levels of the Railway administration

e: The Staff Benefit Fund is administered through Staff Benefit Fund Committees constituted at the prescribed levels, not personally by the General Manager alone.

q: A zonal Railway has to ensure that the orders on reservation for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and Other Backward Classes in services are properly implemented and liaison maintained in the matter. The officer appointed in the administration for this purpose is the:
e: The Liaison Officer is appointed to ensure proper implementation of reservation orders for SC, ST and OBC in services and to maintain liaison in the matter.

q: A railway servant draws pay of Rs 45,000 per month and has a balance of Rs 5,00,000 at his credit in the General Provident Fund. He applies for a temporary (refundable) advance from the Fund, which is ordinarily limited to three months' pay or half the amount at his credit, whichever is less. The maximum advance ordinarily admissible to him will be:
e: Temporary GPF advance is limited to three months' pay or half the credit, whichever is less. Three months' pay is Rs 1,35,000, less than Rs 2,50,000, so Rs 1,35,000 is admissible.

q: A railway servant drawing last basic pay of Rs 75,000 per month is transferred in public interest to another station, but the transfer does not involve any change of his residence. The Composite Transfer Grant admissible to him, at 33 per cent of his last basic pay, will be:
e: Composite Transfer Grant without change of residence is 33 per cent of last basic pay. So 33 per cent of Rs 75,000 = Rs 24,750.

q: A railway servant retires on superannuation with 280 days of Leave on Average Pay and 100 days of Leave on Half Average Pay at his credit. His pay plus Dearness Allowance at retirement is Rs 90,000 per month. The total cash equivalent of leave salary payable to him, the shortfall in Leave on Average Pay being made good by encashment of Leave on Half Average Pay at half rate so that the total does not exceed 300 days, will be:
e: LAP encashment is 280 x Rs 3,000 = Rs 8,40,000. The 20-day shortfall from LHAP at half rate is 20 x Rs 1,500 = Rs 30,000, giving a total of Rs 8,70,000 for 300 days.

q: A railway servant dies while in service after completing 16 years of qualifying service. His emoluments at the time of death are Rs 47,000 per month. The death gratuity payable to his family, at 12 times his emoluments as admissible for this length of service, will be:
e: Death gratuity for 5 to 20 years of qualifying service is 12 times emoluments. So for 16 years, 12 x Rs 47,000 = Rs 5,64,000.

q: A railway servant retires on superannuation under the Unified Pension Scheme after rendering 24 years of qualifying service. His last drawn basic pay is Rs 55,000 per month and Dearness Allowance is admissible at 50 per cent of basic pay. The lump sum payment admissible to him, at one-tenth of his last drawn basic pay plus Dearness Allowance for every completed six-monthly period of qualifying service, will be:
e: UPS lump sum is one-tenth of last basic pay plus DA per six-monthly period. One-tenth of Rs 82,500 is Rs 8,250, and for 48 periods it is Rs 3,96,000.

q: A pay clerk proposes to disburse the pay and allowances of the staff of his office for a month on the seventh day of the following month, on the analogy of the wage-payment rules applicable to workshop staff. The correct position under the establishment rules is that the pay and allowances for a month are ordinarily disbursed on:

options.A: The seventh day of the next month in all cases
options.B: The last working day of the same month
options.C: The first working day of the next month
options.D: The last working day of the next month

e: Pay and allowances for a month are ordinarily disbursed on the last working day of the same month under the establishment rules.

q: A railway servant is appointed to another post in the same station, and the appointment does not involve the assumption of duties and responsibilities of greater importance than those of the post already held by him. His pay in the new post is fixed:

options.A: At the stage equal to the pay drawn by him in the old post, and if there is no such stage, at the next higher stage
options.B: At the minimum of the pay level of the new post in all cases
options.C: At the stage next below the pay drawn by him in the old post
options.D: By granting him one increment in the new post in all cases

e: Where the new post carries no greater importance, pay is fixed at the stage equal to pay in the old post, and if there is no such stage, at the next higher stage.

q: A railway servant in receipt of high emoluments wishes to subscribe to the General Provident Fund at a monthly rate far above the prescribed minimum of 6 per cent of his emoluments. The maximum amount of monthly subscription that he may pay into the Fund shall not exceed:

options.C: Rs 5 lakh in a financial year

e: GPF subscription must be at least 6 per cent of emoluments and shall not exceed the subscriber's total emoluments, as per the GPF Rules.

q: A railway servant posted at a hill station applies for the Warm Clothing Advance for the purchase of warm clothing, relying on the practice followed before the 7th Central Pay Commission. The correct position under the 7th CPC dispensation is that the Warm Clothing Advance has been:

options.A: Enhanced to twice the amount admissible earlier
options.D: Merged with the House Building Advance

e: The Warm Clothing Advance has been abolished under the 7th CPC dispensation, so it is no longer admissible at a hill station.

q: A railway servant drawing basic pay of Rs 46,000 per month is posted in a city classified as 'X' class for the purpose of House Rent Allowance. Dearness Allowance admissible to railway servants has crossed 50 per cent, so that House Rent Allowance in an 'X' class city is payable at 30 per cent of basic pay. The House Rent Allowance admissible to him per month will be:
e: For an X class city, HRA is 30 per cent of basic pay when DA has crossed 50 per cent. So 30 per cent of Rs 46,000 = Rs 13,800.

q: A railway servant is on tour for a day and is provided with free boarding only by the Government, the lodging being arranged and paid for by himself. The admissible rate of Daily Allowance for the station is Rs 1,400 per day. The Daily Allowance admissible to him for that day, at 50 per cent of the admissible rate, will be:
e: When only free boarding is provided on tour, DA is admissible at 50 per cent of the rate. So 50 per cent of Rs 1,400 = Rs 700.

q: A woman railway servant with disability is in receipt of the Special Allowance for Child Care at the revised rate of Rs 3,750 per month in respect of her youngest child. The total amount of the allowance admissible to her for a period of four months will be:
e: Special Allowance for Child Care for a woman with disability is Rs 3,750 per month for the youngest child. For four months it is 4 x Rs 3,750 = Rs 15,000.

q: A railway pensioner who has been granted pension on account of 100 per cent disablement and requires the services of an attendant is in receipt of Constant Attendant Allowance at the rate of Rs 8,438 per month. The total amount of the allowance admissible to him for a quarter, that is, for three months, will be:
e: Constant Attendant Allowance at Rs 8,438 per month for three months is 3 x Rs 8,438 = Rs 25,314 for the quarter.

q: A railway pensioner surrenders Rs 2,500 per month of his pension for commutation. Taking the commutation value for his age on the next birthday as 8.446 for each rupee of annual pension commuted, the lump sum commuted value payable to him will be:
e: Lump sum commuted value is monthly pension surrendered x 12 x factor. So Rs 2,500 x 12 x 8.446 = Rs 2,53,380.

q: A railway servant is selected to participate in a mountaineering expedition approved by the Indian Mountaineering Foundation and applies for Special Casual Leave for the purpose. Such leave can be granted to him up to:
e: Special Casual Leave for an approved mountaineering expedition can be granted up to 30 days in a calendar year.

q: A railway servant is transferred in public interest and, in special circumstances, an extension of his joining time is proposed by the competent authority. The joining time admissible to him, including any such extension, shall not exceed:
e: Joining time on transfer in public interest, including any extension granted in special circumstances, shall not exceed 30 days in total.

q: A railway pensioner settled abroad fails to draw his pension for a continuous period of more than one year and thereafter approaches the pension disbursing authority for payment. The correct position is that the pension:

options.A: Is forfeited permanently to the Government
options.B: Ceases to be payable and can be resumed only with the sanction of the competent authority
options.C: Continues to accumulate and is paid in full, on demand, at any time thereafter
options.D: Is transferred to the credit of the Staff Benefit Fund

e: Pension not drawn for more than one year ceases to be payable and can be resumed only with the sanction of the competent authority.

q: The widow of a deceased railway servant, who is in receipt of family pension, applies for commutation of a portion of her family pension for a lump sum payment. Her application is liable to be rejected because commutation of pension for a lump sum payment is NOT admissible in the case of:
e: Commutation for a lump sum payment is not admissible in the case of family pension, though it is admissible for service pensions such as superannuation pension.

q: A retired railway servant is himself in receipt of a pension for his own service. His wife, who was also a railway servant, dies, and family pension becomes admissible to him in respect of her service. In regard to the two pensions, the correct position is that he:

options.A: Can draw only the higher of the two pensions
options.B: Must surrender his own pension in order to draw the family pension
options.C: Can draw both his own pension and the family pension admissible in respect of his deceased spouse at the same time
options.D: Can draw only his own pension, the family pension not being admissible to him

e: A pensioner can draw both his own pension and the family pension admissible in respect of his deceased spouse at the same time.

q: A railway servant disappears and his whereabouts are not known. His family lodges a report with the police and fulfils the other prescribed conditions. The family becomes eligible for the grant of family pension and other retirement benefits on the expiry of:

options.A: Six months from the date of his disappearance
options.B: Two years from the date of his disappearance
options.C: Seven years from the date of his disappearance
options.D: One year from the date of his disappearance

e: Family pension and retirement benefits for a missing railway servant become eligible to the family on expiry of one year from the date of disappearance, after a police report and other conditions.

q: A subscriber to the National Pension System exits from the system on attaining the age of 60 years, and his total accumulated pension wealth is Rs 4,20,000, which does not exceed Rs 5 lakh. In regard to the utilisation of that wealth, the correct position is that he is permitted to:

options.A: Withdraw only 40 per cent of the corpus as a lump sum, the balance being utilised for purchase of an annuity
options.B: Withdraw the entire accumulated pension wealth as a lump sum, without purchasing any annuity
options.C: Withdraw only 20 per cent of the corpus as a lump sum
options.D: Withdraw nothing until the corpus exceeds Rs 5 lakh

e: On NPS exit at 60, if total accumulated wealth does not exceed Rs 5 lakh, here Rs 4,20,000, the entire amount may be withdrawn as lump sum without annuity purchase.

q: A subscriber to the National Pension System, who has already made three partial withdrawals from his Tier-I account before attaining the age of 60 years, applies for a fourth partial withdrawal for a permissible purpose. His application is liable to be rejected because the maximum number of partial withdrawals permitted to a subscriber from his Tier-I account before attaining the age of 60 years is:
e: A maximum of three partial withdrawals from the NPS Tier-I account is permitted before attaining the age of 60, so a fourth is not admissible.

q: A subscriber exiting from the National Pension System is required to purchase an annuity for providing pension to him out of the prescribed portion of his accumulated pension wealth. The annuity is purchased from:

options.A: An Annuity Service Provider empanelled by the Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority
options.B: The Life Insurance Corporation of India only
options.C: Any insurance company of the choice of the subscriber
options.D: The Accounts Office of the Railway in which he last served

e: Annuity on NPS exit is purchased from an Annuity Service Provider empanelled by the Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority.

q: A railway servant covered under the National Pension System wishes to exercise the option for the Unified Pension Scheme, and a doubt arises in his office about the date from which the Scheme was introduced as such an option. The Unified Pension Scheme came into effect from:
e: The Unified Pension Scheme as an option for NPS subscribers came into effect from 1st April, 2025.

q: An accounts clerk is required to distinguish between the two kinds of gratuity payable to a railway servant on his retirement in different situations. Which of the following correctly distinguishes 'service gratuity' from 'retirement gratuity'?

options.A: Service gratuity is payable in addition to pension, whereas retirement gratuity is payable in lieu of pension
options.B: Both service gratuity and retirement gratuity are payable at the same rate and on the same conditions
options.C: Service gratuity is payable only on the death of a railway servant in service, whereas retirement gratuity is payable only on superannuation
options.D: Service gratuity is paid in lieu of pension to a railway servant retiring with less than ten years of qualifying service, at the rate of half a month's emoluments for each completed six-monthly period of qualifying service, whereas retirement gratuity is paid in addition to pension, at the rate of one-fourth of a month's emoluments for each completed six-monthly period, to a railway servant who has completed not less than five years of qualifying service

e: Service gratuity is paid in lieu of pension for less than ten years of service at half a month per period, while retirement gratuity is paid in addition to pension at one-fourth per period after at least five years.

q: A doubt arises in an office whether the retirement of a railway servant ordered in public interest under the relevant retirement rules is a punishment, like compulsory retirement imposed after disciplinary proceedings. Which of the following correctly distinguishes 'compulsory retirement' from 'premature retirement' of a railway servant?

options.A: Compulsory retirement is ordered in public interest under the retirement rules, whereas premature retirement is a penalty under the Discipline and Appeal Rules
options.B: Compulsory retirement is a major penalty imposed after disciplinary proceedings, whereas premature retirement ordered in public interest under the relevant retirement rules is not a penalty
options.C: There is no distinction between compulsory retirement and premature retirement
options.D: Premature retirement carries no pensionary benefits, whereas compulsory retirement carries full pensionary benefits in all cases

e: Compulsory retirement is a major penalty imposed after disciplinary proceedings, whereas premature retirement in public interest under the retirement rules is not a penalty.

q: A railway servant retires on superannuation and settles down at his home town, but avails the Travelling Allowance for the journey of himself and his family to that place fourteen months after the date of his retirement. His claim is liable to be rejected because the Travelling Allowance admissible on retirement can be availed of within:

options.A: Three months from the date of his retirement
options.B: Six months from the date of his retirement
options.C: One year from the date of his retirement
options.D: Two years from the date of his retirement

e: Travelling Allowance on retirement for settling at the home town can be availed of within one year from the date of retirement, so a claim at fourteen months is late.

q: An order placing a railway servant under suspension was passed by his disciplinary authority. The same authority later proposes to revoke the order while the disciplinary proceedings are still pending. The correct position is that an order of suspension may be revoked at any time by:

options.A: The authority which made the order, or any authority to which that authority is subordinate
options.D: The Inquiring Authority appointed in the case

e: An order of suspension may be revoked at any time by the authority which made it, or any authority to which that authority is subordinate.

q: A railway servant seeks permission to join an association of employees whose objects, as set out in its constitution, are found to be prejudicial to public order. Under Rule 6 of the Railway Services (Conduct) Rules, 1966, he shall not join, or continue to be a member of, an association:

options.A: Which is not registered as a trade union
options.B: Which does not restrict its membership to railway servants only
options.C: Which has not been recognised by the Railway Administration
options.D: The objects or activities of which are prejudicial to the interests of the sovereignty and integrity of India, public order or morality

e: Rule 6 of the Conduct Rules, 1966 bars joining an association whose objects or activities are prejudicial to sovereignty and integrity of India, public order or morality.

q: The son of a railway servant takes part in a movement which is subversive of the State, and the railway servant, despite his best efforts, is unable to prevent him from doing so. Under Rule 5 of the Railway Services (Conduct) Rules, 1966, the railway servant shall, in such a situation:

options.B: Make a report in that behalf to the Government
options.C: Merely inform his immediate superior officer verbally about it
options.D: Take no action, as the conduct of his family members does not concern him

e: Under Rule 5 of the Conduct Rules, 1966, if a family member takes part in a subversive movement and the servant cannot prevent it, he shall make a report to the Government.

q: A railway servant behaves in a public place in a manner which, though not amounting to a breach of any specific service rule, brings discredit to the service. His conduct is in breach of Rule 3(1)(iii) of the Railway Services (Conduct) Rules, 1966, which requires every railway servant at all times to:

options.C: Do nothing which is unbecoming of a railway servant

e: Rule 3(1)(iii) of the Conduct Rules, 1966 requires every railway servant at all times to do nothing which is unbecoming of a railway servant.

q: A railway servant marries a person having a nationality other than Indian. Under the Railway Services (Conduct) Rules, 1966, he is required, in regard to that marriage, to:

options.A: Intimate the fact to the Government forthwith
options.B: Obtain the prior permission of the Government for the marriage
options.C: Resign from railway service before such marriage
options.D: Report the marriage to the prescribed authority within a period of one year

e: A railway servant marrying a person of non-Indian nationality must intimate the fact to the Government forthwith under the Conduct Rules, 1966.

q: In a disciplinary case, the disciplinary authority proposes to close the matter by issuing a 'warning' to the railway servant, treating it as one of the penalties under the Railway Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules. The correct position is that the penalty which is NOT specified in those Rules is:

options.B: Recovery from pay of the whole or part of any pecuniary loss caused to the Railways

e: Warning is not a penalty specified in the Railway Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, unlike censure, recovery from pay and withholding of increments.

q: A disciplinary authority imposes on a railway servant the penalty of withholding of his promotion for a specified period. This penalty is classified under the Railway Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules as a:

options.C: Penalty imposable only by the President
options.D: Penalty not included in the Rules

e: Withholding of promotion for a specified period is classified as a minor penalty under the Railway Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules.

q: For the purpose of computing the number of days on which an employee has worked in an establishment in an accounting year under Section 14 of the Payment of Bonus Act, 1965, a doubt arises about the days on which he was on leave with salary. Under that section, the employee shall be deemed to have worked on the days on which he has:

options.A: Remained absent without leave for any reason whatsoever
options.B: Participated in a strike declared illegal under the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947
options.C: Been laid off, been on leave with salary or wages, been absent due to temporary disablement caused by an employment injury, or been on maternity leave with salary or wages
options.D: Remained absent on account of his detention in police custody in a criminal case

e: Under Section 14 of the Payment of Bonus Act, 1965, days of lay-off, leave with salary, absence due to employment injury disablement and maternity leave with salary count as days worked.
